sources.title: A. Björner and F. Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups, GTM 231 (class-hosted complete PDF)
sources.locator: Complete 370-page author/class-hosted text; read in the run's extracted full text for: Chapter 7.1, printed pp. 201-208 (Poincare series, Lemmas 7.1.1-7.1.2, Proposition 7.1.3, Corollary 7.1.4, Theorem 7.1.5, Example 7.1.6, Proposition 7.1.7); Chapter 2.3, printed pp. 36-37 (Propositions 2.3.1-2.3.2); Chapter 2.4, printed pp. 38-43 (parabolic subgroups, Proposition 2.4.4); Chapter 3.2, printed pp. 70-72 (Lemma 3.2.3); Chapter 8.1-8.2, printed pp. 245-252 (signed and even-signed permutation models, Propositions 8.1.1-8.1.3). Reading record: research/coxeter-scaffold/combinatorial-source-report.md.

contents.name: Section 7.1 (pp. 201-203): definition of the Poincare series $A(q)=\sum_{w\in A}q^{\ell(w)}$, finiteness of length fibers for finite $S$, the descent-class sets $D^J_I$, Lemma 7.1.1 (reducible factorization), Lemma 7.1.2 ($W(q)=W^J(q)W_J(q)$), Proposition 7.1.3 (descent-class inclusion-exclusion)
Section 7.1 (pp. 203-204): Corollary 7.1.4(i)-(ii): the Steinberg identity in the finite case and the vanishing identity in the infinite case
Section 2.3 (pp. 36-37): Proposition 2.3.1(ii) (an element with all left descents forces finiteness and equals $w_0$) and Proposition 2.3.2(ii),(iv) (length complement and $\ell(w_0)=|T|$)
Section 2.4 (pp. 39-43): minimal coset representatives $W^J$ and the length-additive factorization $W=W^JW_J$ (Proposition 2.4.4)
Section 3.2 (pp. 71-72): Lemma 3.2.3: $J$ has an upper bound in weak order if and only if $W_J$ is finite, and then the join is $w_0(J)$
Section 7.1 (pp. 204-205): Theorem 7.1.5 (the exponent product $W(q)=\prod_i[e_i+1]_q$), formula (7.5) (the type-$A$ product) and the type-$B/D$ route via signed permutations
Section 7.1, Example 7.1.6 (p. 205): the exact normal-form computation for $F_4$, $W^{S\setminus\{s_4\}}(q)=1+q+q^2+q^3+2(q^4+\cdots+q^{11})+q^{12}+q^{13}+q^{14}+q^{15}=[8]_q(1+q^4+q^8)$
Section 7.1 (pp. 206-208): Proposition 7.1.7, the Mobius/nerve formula $1/W(q)=-\sum_{K\in N}\mu_N(K,S)/W_K(q)$ for infinite $W$
contents.reason: The run's route computes rational growth from Corollary 7.1.4(ii) and the denominator recursion (Davis Corollary 17.1.6) directly; the nerve/Mobius refinement is not needed for any item of this pair and would add the simplicial-complex machinery of the nerve without a consumer.

contents.name: Section 7.1 (pp. 207-208): formula 7.1.10, Bott's formula for the growth series of affine Weyl groups
contents.reason: Bott’s affine growth formula is outside this approved growth pair: it proves finite Poincare exponent products, general rationality by descent/parabolic recursion, and the infinite-dihedral example. The selected affine pairs prove alcove geometry and diagram classification, not an additional affine enumeration theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 8.1, printed pp. 246-248: signed-permutation model and generators, Proposition 8.1.1 with the complete proof of the length formula, and Proposition 8.1.3 identifying the Coxeter system; Chapter 8.2, printed pp. 252-255: even-signed model and generators and Proposition 8.2.1 with the complete length proof. The book's sign node and fork numbering differ from this item; its model and length arguments were checked as convention comparisons, while the item proves its own coordinate models and Schreier graphs.
Sections 8.1-8.2 (pp. 245-252): the same models used for the insertion recursions $P_{B_n}=[2n]_tP_{B_{n-1}}$, $P_{D_n}=[n]_t(1+t^{n-1})P_{D_{n-1}}$

sources.locator: Complete 600-page author manuscript; read in the extracted full text for: Chapter 4.6-4.7, printed pp. 51-54 (Lemmas 4.6.1-4.6.2, Definition 4.7.1, Lemma 4.7.2, Lemma 4.7.3); Chapter 17.1, printed pp. 315-319 (Lemmas 17.1.1-17.1.4, Corollaries 17.1.5-17.1.6, Lemma 17.1.7); Chapter 17.2, printed pp. 319-321 (Bott's affine formula); Chapter 17.3-17.4 (growth series of type HM and Coxeter elements).

contents.name: Lemma 4.7.2 (p. 53): for every $w\in W$ the special subgroup $W_{\operatorname{In}(w)}$ is finite (the finite-descent-parabolic lemma), with Lemma 4.6.2 and Lemma 4.3.1 as its inputs

Definition 4.7.1 and Lemma 4.7.3 (pp. 52-54): $\operatorname{In}(w)$ is the set of ending letters of a reduced expression; $w$ is the longest element of $wW_{\operatorname{In}(w)}$ and the shortest of $wW_{\operatorname{Out}(w)}$
Lemma 17.1.1 (p. 316): $W(t)=t_SW(t^{-1})$ for finite $W$ (reciprocity)
Lemma 17.1.2 (p. 316): $W(t)=B_T(t)W_T(t)$ for each $T\subseteq S$, the parabolic factorization in the coset form
Lemmas 17.1.3-17.1.4 (pp. 317): Mobius inversion and the descent-class formula $W_T(t)=W(t)\sum_{U\subseteq T}\varepsilon(T-U)/W_{S-U}(t)$
Corollary 17.1.5 (pp. 317-318): $t_S=W(t)\sum_{T\subseteq S}\varepsilon(T)/W_T(t)$ for finite $W$ and $0=\sum_{T\subseteq S}\varepsilon(T)/W_T(t)$ for infinite $W$
Corollary 17.1.6 (p. 318): rationality $W(t)=f(t)/g(t)$ by induction on $\operatorname{Card}(S)$
Lemma 17.1.7 (pp. 318-319): the coset representatives $B'_T=\{w:T\subseteq\operatorname{In}(w)\}$ of $W/W_T$
Chapter 17.2 (Bott's formula for the growth series of affine Weyl groups)
contents.reason: Bott’s affine growth formula is outside this approved growth pair: it proves finite Poincare exponent products, general rationality by descent/parabolic recursion, and the infinite-dihedral example. The selected affine pairs prove alcove geometry and diagram classification, not an additional affine enumeration theorem.
